title: Slimline Unicode prefetch shim to reduce prompt-prep tail latency
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: In high-concurrency prefill paths we observe 95th/99th tail due to expensive UTF-8 normalization + per-session locale checks before tokenization. Current prefill pipeline performs full unicode normalization (NFKC) and several regex passes for control characters even for short prompts, which inflates CPU time and backpressure on the prefill thread pool.

Goal: Implement a slimline prefetch shim that fast-paths common cases (ASCII + common punctuation) through a lightweight byte-level sanitizer, performs cheap heuristic checks to decide if full normalization is required, and uses a small in-memory prefix cache keyed by (client_id, recent_prompt_prefix_hash) to avoid repeated work for interactive sessions. This should reduce median and tail prefill latency, lower CPU consumption on the prefill pool, and preserve correctness for inputs that require full normalization.

Approach:
- Add a tiny fastpath sanitizer in the ingest hot path that does: (1) quick ASCII-check, (2) single-pass removal of zero-width/control characters, (3) map common curly quotes to ASCII equivalents. If the heuristic fails (non-ASCII, or contains combining marks), escalate to the existing normalization pipeline.
- Implement a size-bounded LRU cache (per-session shard) storing canonicalized prefix->tokenization hints (partial tokenized prefix and a small KV cache pointer). Use weak TTLs to avoid stale state across model rollouts.
- Introduce a safe fallback instrumentation mode where we shadow-run the full normalization for a percentage of requests and assert equivalence; run this for 2 weeks before full rollout.
- Add kernel-hint metadata in the prefill output so downstream scheduler can prioritize decode lanes for cached prefixes.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Fastpath heuristics must be conservative; any deviation that changes tokens for real workloads will roll back. We accept slightly lower hit-rate in cache rather than risking incorrect tokenization.
- Memory budget for LRU caches must be kept per-GPU-process; we will start with 16MB per-shard and monitor.
- The shim increases code complexity in the hot path; need careful benchmarking and canary rollout in Dedicated clusters first.

Deliverables: implementation, unit tests, benchmark harness (local and perf cluster), canary rollout plan, and dashboard for hit-rate and equivalence check failures.
acceptance_criteria: Median prefill CPU time reduced by >= 20% on representative short-prompt workload
95th prefill latency reduced by >= 15% on interactive session traces
Cache hit-rate >= 30% for interactive session replay workload in perf cluster
Does not change tokenization output for verified equivalence sample suite
